relevance_reason: Reports three new FHH3 probands with AP2S1 Arg15 mutations, in vitro rescue by cinacalcet, and clinical response to cinacalcet treatment.

findings.statement: Howles et al. (2016) described 3 unrelated probands with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type 3 (FHH3) and heterozygous AP2S1 mutations: a 34-year-old woman with a 12-year history of hypercalcemia who had fatigue, headaches, and persistent generalized aches that did not resolve after parathyroidectomy; a 22-year-old man with hypercalcemia, fatigue, and generalized rib pain; and a 52-year-old woman with an approximately 20-year history of hypercalcemia who had headaches, abdominal pain, vomiting, fatigue, and musculoskeletal pain that did not resolve after pamidronate infusion or parathyroidectomy.
quotes: The probands included a 34-year-old woman who had a 12-year history of hypercalcemia. She presented with fatigue, headaches, and persistent generalized aches that did not resolve after parathyroidectomy.

In addition, a 22-year-old man presented with hypercalcemia, fatigue, and generalized rib pain, and a 52-year-old woman who had an approximately 20-year history of hypercalcemia presented with headaches, abdominal pain, vomiting, fatigue, and musculoskeletal pain

findings.statement: Howles et al. (2016) identified a heterozygous AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys (R15C) substitution in 1 of 3 unrelated probands with FHH3.
quotes: Each of the three probands had an AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution (Fig. 1A).

findings.statement: Howles et al. (2016) identified a heterozygous AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15His (R15H) substitution in 1 of 3 unrelated probands with FHH3.
quotes: Each of the three probands had an AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution (Fig. 1A).

findings.statement: Howles et al. (2016) identified a heterozygous AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Leu (R15L) substitution in 1 of 3 unrelated probands with FHH3.
quotes: Each of the three probands had an AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution (Fig. 1A).

findings.statement: Howles et al. (2016) found that cinacalcet (10 nM) corrected the abnormal intracellular calcium signaling and MAPK responses to extracellular calcium in cells expressing the calcium-sensing receptor and the Cys15, His15, or Leu15 AP2-sigma mutants, indicating that allosteric modulation of CASR can correct the loss of function caused by AP2S1 mutations.
quotes: Cinacalcet (at a concentration of 10 nM) corrected the abnormal intracellular calcium signaling and MAPK responses to extracellular calcium in cells expressing the Cys15, His15, or Leu15 AP2-sigma mutants
Our results show that cinacalcet-mediated allosteric modulation of the calcium-sensing receptor can correct the loss of function of AP2S1 mutations.

findings.statement: Howles et al. (2016) treated 3 FHH3 probands with oral cinacalcet (30 to 60 mg daily) over 33 to 45 months, resulting in more than 20% reductions in serum calcium and abatement of symptoms; serum phosphate increased and PTH decreased, remaining within the normal range. No nausea, vomiting, or hypocalcemia developed, although the authors noted that long-term surveillance would be required.
quotes: Oral cinacalcet (at a dose of 30 to 60 mg daily) was administered to the three probands with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type 3 over a 33-to-45-month period. This treatment led to more than 20% reductions in serum calcium concentrations (Fig. 1B) and abatement of symptoms.
Adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, and hypocalcemia did not develop in any of the probands.

relevance_reason: Case report of an infant with an AP2S1 p.Arg15Leu mutation (FHH3), describing hypercalciuria and the effect of treatment with low-calcium formula.

findings.statement: Fujisawa et al. (2013) reported a Japanese female infant with FHH3. Hypercalcemia was found on a routine laboratory test done for poor weight gain on breast feeding. At 49 days of age, her adjusted serum calcium was 13.1 mg/dL, intact PTH was 27 pg/mL, and her urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio was 1.29 mg/mg, indicating hypercalciuria rather than hypocalciuria. There was no evidence of hyperparathyroidism, a PTHrP-producing neoplasm, or vitamin D excess.
quotes: This Japanese female infant was found to have hypercalcemia by a routine laboratory test for poor weight gain on breast feeding.
At 49 days of age, serum calcium (adjusted by Payne's formula) was 13.1 mg/dL, intact PTH 27 pg/mL, and urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio 1.29 mg/mg.
There was no evidence for hyperparathyroidism, PTHrP-producing neoplasm, and vitamin D excess.

findings.statement: In a Japanese infant with hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria, Fujisawa et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous p.Arg15Leu mutation in the AP2S1 gene. The authors described the mutation as presumably de novo; it had previously been reported as a cause of FHH3. No pathologic mutation was found in CASR or GNA11.
quotes: Although no pathologic mutation was detected in CASR or GNA11, a presumably de novo heterozygous mutation (p.Arg15Leu), a previously reported causative mutation for FHH3, was identified in AP2S1 of this patient.

findings.statement: Fujisawa et al. (2013) concluded that the absence of hypocalciuria does not necessarily argue against an AP2S1 mutation. They suggested that the patient's early infantile age played a role in her hypercalciuria.
quotes: The results imply that lack of hypocalciuria does not necessarily argue against the presence of AP2S1 mutations.
The early infantile age of this patient would have played a certain role in the occurrence of hypercalciuria

findings.statement: Fujisawa et al. (2013) treated the infant with a low-calcium formula containing 2.6 mg/dL of calcium. She showed catch-up growth, and both her serum calcium and her urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio fell. Feeding a 2:1 mixture of low-calcium and standard formula then kept her serum calcium at about 12 mg/dL without markedly raising serum PTH. The authors concluded that low-calcium formula is worth trying in infants with FHH.
quotes: With use of low calcium formula containing 2.6 mg/dL of calcium, she showed catch-up growth, and serum calcium was decreased, as was urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio.
feeding with a mixture of low calcium formula and standard formula with a 2:1 ratio maintained serum calcium ∼12 mg/dL without markedly increasing serum PTH.
low calcium formula is worth attempting in infants with FHH.

relevance_reason: Identifies AP2S1 Arg15 missense mutations as the cause of FHH3, with families, a cohort screen and functional studies.

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) performed exome sequencing on 1 affected individual from each of 2 unrelated FHH3 kindreds, FHH3OK (Oklahoma) and FHH3NI (Northern Ireland). Within the 3.46-Mb FHH3 interval on 19q13.3, which contains about 110 genes, both patients had only 1 shared variant: a C-to-T transition in exon 2 of the AP2S1 gene, predicting an arg15-to-cys (R15C) substitution. The variant was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Restriction enzyme analysis showed that it cosegregated with the disorder in members from 4 generations of the 2 kindreds.
quotes: An analysis of SNVs within the 3.46Mbp interval on 19q13.3, which is the location of the FHH3 locus, and contains ~110 genes, revealed one SNV, a C to T transition in exon 2 of the AP2S1 gene, which encodes the protein AP2σ2, in patients from both kindreds.
The C to T transition, which predicted the occurrence of a missense mutation (Arg15Cys) (Supplementary Fig. 1), was confirmed by dideoxynucleotide sequencing
were used to demonstrate its cosegregation in members (32 affected and 23 unaffected) from 4 generations of the two kindreds

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) stated that the FHH3 locus lies on chromosome 19q13.3, in a 3.46-Mb interval containing about 110 genes. By comparison, the FHH1 locus is on 3q21.1 and the FHH2 locus is on 19p.
quotes: The loci for FHH1, FHH2, and FHH3 are located on chromosomes 3q21.1, 19p, and 19q13.3, respectively

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) described FHH3 as a disorder of extracellular calcium homeostasis. Unlike FHH1 and FHH2, which usually have normal PTH levels, FHH3 is characterized by increased serum PTH concentrations, hypophosphatemia and osteomalacia. Patients with AP2S1 mutations were aged from 8 days to 78 years. They had elevated serum calcium and PTH and reduced urinary calcium excretion. In the FHHOK kindred, mean serum calcium was 2.88 mmol/l and mean phosphate was 0.77 mmol/l.
quotes: FHH3 is characterised by different clinical features, which include increased serum PTH concentrations, hypophosphatemia, and osteomalacia,.
Patients with these AP2S1 mutations, whose ages ranged from 8 days to 78 years (Table 1), had similar elevations in serum calcium and PTH concentrations and reductions in urine calcium excretion

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) sequenced AP2S1 in 50 unrelated FHH patients (23 males and 27 females) in whom CASR mutations had been excluded. They found 11 heterozygous missense mutations, all affecting arg15: 4 R15C, 3 R15H and 4 R15L. The authors concluded that this was consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance and that AP2S1 Arg15 mutations may cause FHH in more than 20% of patients without CASR mutations.
quotes: This revealed the occurrence of 11 missense heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of FHH3, that all affected Arg15 and consisted of four Arg15Cys, three Arg15His, and four Arg15Leu mutations
Indeed, Arg15 AP2S1 missense mutations may be the underlying cause of FHH in >20% of patients without CaSR mutations.

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) found the AP2S1 R15H mutation (CGC-to-CAC) in 3 unrelated FHH probands who were negative for CASR mutations. These were 2 females aged 19 and 49 years and 1 male aged 73 years at diagnosis, with serum calcium levels of 2.62 to 2.85 mmol/l.
quotes: Arg15His (CGC→CAC)
three Arg15His

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) found the AP2S1 R15L mutation (CGC-to-CTC) in 4 unrelated FHH probands or families who were negative for CASR mutations. In one of these, diagnosis was made at 0.02 years of age. Serum calcium levels ranged from 3.03 to 3.3 mmol/l.
quotes: Arg15Leu (CGC→CTC)

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) found that patients with the R15C, R15H and R15L mutations had similar elevations in serum calcium and PTH and similar reductions in urinary calcium. This indicated no correlation between mutation and clinical phenotype.
quotes: had similar elevations in serum calcium and PTH concentrations and reductions in urine calcium excretion, thereby indicating an absence of a correlation between the mutation and clinical phenotype.

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) found 3 different mutations affecting only arg15 in 13 unrelated probands, and noted that arg15 is significantly conserved in 5,400 human exomes (p less than 10(-10)). They concluded that this residue is likely a mutational hotspot.
quotes: the occurrence of these 3 different AP2S1 mutations that altered only the Arg15 residue in 13 unrelated probands and the significant conservation of the Arg15 residue in 5,400 human exomes (p<10−10, Fisher exact test) indicates that this residue represents a likely mutational hotspot.

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) noted that FHH1, FHH2 and FHH3 are genetically heterogeneous autosomal dominant disorders. About 65% of FHH patients have FHH1, caused by CASR loss-of-function mutations, and AP2S1 mutations accounted for more than 20% of the remaining cases.
quotes: FHH3, together with FHH1 and FHH2 are genetically heterogenous autosomal dominant disorders of extracellular-calcium (Cao2+) homeostasis
Approximately 65% of FHH patients have FHH1, due to loss-of-function mutations of the CaSR, a GPCR encoded by a gene on 3q21.1-.

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) noted that arg15 is conserved across AP2-sigma-2 orthologs and in human AP sigma paralogs. Crystal structure analysis showed that arg15 forms key contacts with a glutamine at position -4 of the dileucine motifs of cargo proteins. The authors predicted that the R15C and R15L substitutions would reduce affinity for the dileucine motif. They noted that CaSR contains a C-terminal dileucine motif (RHQPLL, residues 1009-1014).
quotes: an analysis of the crystal structure of AP2 revealed that the Arg15 (R15) residue of AP2σ2 and the Arg21 (R21) residue of AP2α1 are involved in forming key contacts with a glutamine (Q) residue at position −4 relative to the first leucine of the dileucine motif of cargo proteins
the CaSR has within its cytoplasmic C-terminal domain a variant dileucine motif (Arg-His-Gln-Pro-Leu-Leu (RHQPLL), residues 1009-1014)

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) expressed mutant AP2S1 in HEK293 cells stably expressing CaSR. All 3 mutants (R15C, R15H, R15L) shifted the concentration-response curves to the right, with a higher EC50 for extracellular calcium than wild type (2.73-2.90 mM vs 2.53 mM). This indicated decreased sensitivity to extracellular calcium. The R15C mutant raised the EC50 above that of vector alone, which suggested a possible dominant-negative effect.
quotes: This revealed that expression of all three mutant AP2σ2s led to a rightward shift in the concentration–response curves (Fig. 3c-e) with significantly higher EC50

whereas the EC50 value of cells transfected with the Cys15 AP2S1 mutant were significantly higher than those with vector alone, thereby indicating a possible dominant-negative effect for this AP2S1 mutant

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) measured cell-surface CaSR by intact-cell ELISA. After stimulation with extracellular calcium, cells transfected with wild-type AP2S1 had a greater reduction in surface CaSR than cells transfected with the R15C mutant. This indicated reduced CaSR endocytosis with the mutant. Separately, replacing the CaSR dileucine motif (Leu-Leu1013-1014 to Ala-Ala) also raised the EC50, indicating that the motif is functionally significant.
quotes: cells transfected with wild-type AP2S1 had a significantly further reduction of cell-surface CaSR expression when compared to those transfected with mutant Arg15Cys AP2S1 or vector alone
Thus, these results indicate that the CaSR dileucine motif is functionally significant.

relevance_reason: Reports a second FHH3 kindred, its clinical features, and linkage that narrows the FHH3 locus on 19q13.3.

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2010) studied a kindred in which the proband was a 43-year-old woman. She had a corrected serum calcium of 2.74 mmol/l (normal, 2.15-2.55), a serum PTH of 47 pg/ml (normal, 10-65), and a urinary calcium clearance:creatinine clearance ratio of 0.006. She had no CASR mutation in the coding region or splice sites. Of 24 members from 3 generations of her kindred, 16 were hypercalcemic with normal or elevated serum PTH and mild hypophosphatemia, features the authors considered consistent with FHH3.
quotes: The proband was a 43-yr-old woman who presented with a corrected serum calcium of 2.74 mmol/liter (normal = 2.15-2.55 mmol/liter), a serum PTH of 47 pg/ml (normal = 10-65 pg/ml), and a urinary calcium clearance:creatinine clearance of 0.006.
Sixteen members were hypercalcemic with normal or elevated serum PTH concentrations and mild hypophosphatemia, features consistent with FHH3.

findings.statement: In this kindred, Nesbit et al. (2010) found that FHH cosegregated with microsatellite and SNP markers from chromosome 19q13.3, with a peak lod score of 5.98 at theta = 0.0 with D19S412. Analysis of recombinants placed the locus in a 3.46-Mb interval between SNP rs1990932 (centromeric) and D19S604 (telomeric).
quotes: Use of microsatellite and single nucleotide polymorphic loci from chromosome 19q13.3 demonstrated cosegregation with FHH in the kindred, with a peak LOD score = 5.98 at 0% recombination with D19S412.
Analysis of recombinants mapped FHH to a 3.46-Mbp interval flanked centromerically by single nucleotide polymorphism rs1990932 and telomerically by D19S604.

findings.statement: Nesbit et al. (2010) noted that FHH is genetically heterogeneous, with 3 types: FHH1 on 3q21.1, FHH2 on 19p, and FHH3 on 19q13. FHH1 is caused by CASR mutations and accounts for more than 65% of patients. The authors suggested that FHH3 may explain the disorder in FHH patients without CASR mutations.
quotes: FHH1, caused by mutations of the calcium-sensing receptor (CASR), occurs in more than 65% of patients, whereas the abnormalities underlying FHH2 and FHH3, which have each been described in single North American kindreds, are unknown.
FHH3 may explain the calcium homeostasis disorder in those FHH patients who do not have CASR mutations.

relevance_reason: Refined mapping of FBHH3 (Oklahoma variant) in the original kindred, plus exclusion of candidate genes in the region.

findings.statement: Hannan et al. (2010) restudied the previously reported Oklahoma kindred with FBHH3 and investigated 40 members from 5 generations. They diagnosed FBHH from hypercalcemia together with a low calcium/creatinine clearance ratio (<0.01). Serum PTH was elevated in some affected individuals older than 30 years, and 3 affected adults older than 40 years had evidence of osteomalacia.
quotes: Forty members, from five generations, of the previously reported FBHHOk kindred were investigated. For these family members, the biochemical phenotype of FBHH was established by documenting hypercalcaemia associated with a low ratio (<0.01) of calcium clearance to creatinine clearance.

Elevated concentrations of serum PTH had been observed in some affected individuals >30 years of age (II.2, II.4, II.6, II.9 and III.6, Figure 1). Three adults >40 years of age (II.4, II.9 and III.3) also showed evidence of osteomalacia.

phenotypes.text: low calcium to creatinine clearance ratio

findings.statement: Hannan et al. (2010) performed linkage analysis in 34 informative members of the Oklahoma kindred (19 affected) using 17 microsatellite markers and 7 SNPs. They confirmed linkage to chromosome 19q13, with a peak 2-point LOD score of 6.92 at theta = 0 for D19S606. Recombinants in 3 individuals refined the FBHH3 locus to a 4.1-Mb interval (<10 cM) flanked by D19S112 and rs245111. The interval contained 135 protein-coding genes and 24 predicted genes.
quotes: Linkage between FBHHOk and 10 of the 14 polymorphic loci (Table 1) from chromosome 19q13 was established with the highest peak LOD score of 6.92, at 0% recombination, being observed between D19S606 and FBHHOk.

Thus, the FBHH3 was mapped to an interval flanked centromerically by D19S112 and telomerically by rs245111. This interval was found to be 4.1 Mb in size and to contain 135 protein-coding genes and 24 predicted genes.
Thus, the 34 family members from five generations included for genetic analysis of the FBHH3 locus consisted of 19 affected members, 13 unaffected members and 2 unaffected spouses (Figure 1).

findings.statement: Hannan et al. (2010) noted that the region of mouse chromosome 7 syntenic to the FBHH3 interval contains 4 Casr-related sequences (Gprc2a-rs genes), but BLAST analysis found no human or primate homologs. Comparison of the human (22.0 Mb) and mouse (39.3 Mb) syntenic regions showed 2 conserved segments that were inverted in man and an 11.6-Mb mouse region, containing 35 genes including the 4 Gprc2a-rs genes, that is absent from the human genome. The authors concluded that FBHH3 cannot be attributed to Gprc2a-rs abnormalities.
quotes: However, a bioinformatic (BLAST) analysis of the human 19q13 region did not identify the human, or primate, homologues of the Gprc2a-rs genes, thereby precluding their mutational analysis for FBHH3.
In addition, an 11.6 Mb region on mouse chromosome 7 that contains 35 murine genes including the four Gprc2a-rs was not present in the human genome (Figure 3).
Thus, FBHH3 cannot be attributed to Gprc2a-rss abnormalities.

findings.statement: Hannan et al. (2010) sequenced the coding regions and intron-exon boundaries of 12 candidate genes from the FBHH3 interval in an affected member of the Oklahoma kindred. The genes (including PTH2, PTGIR, GNG8, EMP3, SPHK2, TULP2, NUCB1, HRC, RCN3, CYTH2, RRAS and ATF5) were chosen for renal and/or parathyroid expression. No abnormalities were found, and RT-PCR excluded splicing defects, indicating that these genes were unlikely to cause FBHH3.
quotes: DNA sequence analysis of the coding region and intron–exon boundaries of these 12 genes, from an individual affected with FBHHOk and from an unrelated normal individual, did not detect any abnormalities. In addition, RT-PCR excluded any splicing abnormalities, thereby indicating that these genes were unlikely to be responsible for FBHHOk.

relevance_reason: The paper maps the Oklahoma variant of familial benign hypercalcemia (FBHOk), the subject of this entry, to chromosome 19q13 and excludes the 3q and 19p loci.

findings.statement: In an Oklahoma family with a variant of familial benign hypercalcemia (FBHOk), Lloyd et al. (1999) carried out a genomewide search using microsatellite polymorphisms. They found linkage to 8 loci on chromosome 19q13, with the highest LOD score of 6.67 at a recombination fraction of 0.00 for D19S606. Recombinants placed the locus in an interval of less than 12 cM flanked by D19S908 and D19S866.
quotes: Linkage was established between FBHOk and eight chromosome 19q13 loci, with the highest LOD score, 6.67 (recombination fraction.00), obtained with D19S606.
Recombinants further mapped FBHOk to a <12-cM interval flanked by D19S908 and D19S866.

findings.statement: Lloyd et al. (1999) reported that linkage of the Oklahoma FBH variant family to the CaSR region on 3q and to the 19p13.3 FBH locus had been excluded. They suggested that a further CaSR or a mediator of calcium homeostasis is involved.
quotes: in an Oklahoma family with an FBH variant (FBHOk), for which linkage to 3q and 19p had been excluded
This mapping of FBHOk to chromosome 19q13 will facilitate the identification of another CaSR or a mediator of calcium homeostasis.

findings.statement: Lloyd et al. (1999) sequenced the calmodulin III gene, which lies within the 19q13 interval, in 1 individual affected with FBHOk. The sequencing covered the coding region, the 5-prime UTR, and part of the promoter, and found no abnormalities. The authors concluded that this gene is unlikely to be involved in FBHOk.
quotes: The calmodulin III gene is located within this interval, and DNA sequence analysis of the coding region, the 5' UTR, and part of the promoter region in an individual affected with FBHOk did not detect any abnormalities

relevance_reason: Defines the Oklahoma variant of FBH (HHC3) in a five-generation kindred and shows by linkage that it is excluded from the known FBH, MEN1 and PTH loci.

findings.statement: Trump et al. (1995) studied a 5-generation kindred from Oklahoma, USA, with 19 affected members, 2 obligate carriers, and 20 unaffected members. In this family, familial benign (hypocalciuric) hypercalcemia (FBH) occurred together with a developmental elevation in serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels.
quotes: A five-generation kindred (19 affected, two obligate carriers and 20 unaffected) from Oklahoma USA, in which familial benign (hypocalciuric) hypercalcaemia (FBH) was associated with a developmental elevation in serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels

phenotypes.text: developmental elevation in serum parathyroid hormone levels

findings.statement: In the Oklahoma kindred, Trump et al. (1995) tested 17 polymorphic markers from candidate regions: 3q21-q24 and 19p13.3 (FBH loci), 11q13 (MEN1), and 11p15 (PTH). Linkage to all of these regions was excluded (lod scores less than -2.00 at theta = 0.05 to 0.25). Analysis of multipoint crossovers and the LINKMAP program confirmed the exclusion.
quotes: By means of 17 polymorphic markers from these regions, linkage was excluded [LOD scores < -2.00 at (theta) = 0.05-0.25].
In addition, an analysis of multipoint crossovers and use of the LINKMAP program confirmed the exclusion from these regions.

findings.statement: Trump et al. (1995) named this form of FBH the Oklahoma variant, FBH(Ok). Because it was not linked to markers that segregate with FBH, MEN1, or PTH, the authors concluded that their results indicated further genetic heterogeneity and a third locus for FBH.
quotes: Thus, this form of FBH, designated the Oklahoma variant FBH(Ok), is not linked to markers that segregate with FBH, MEN1 and PTH; our results indicate further genetic heterogeneity and the presence of a third locus for FBH.

findings.statement: Trump et al. (1995) designated the FBH in the Oklahoma kindred as the Oklahoma variant, FBH(Ok).
quotes: this form of FBH, designated the Oklahoma variant FBH(Ok)

relevance_reason: Describes the large kindred with familial benign hypercalcemia, elevated PTH and osteomalacia that serves as the founding description of this variant (Oklahoma type) of FBH.

findings.statement: McMurtry et al. (1992) described a large kindred with familial benign hypercalcemia (FBH) in which 19 of 46 members studied across 5 generations (ages 1.5 to 91 years) were affected. In the 15 hypercalcemic subjects examined biochemically, serum immunoreactive PTH levels, measured in 3 separate immunoassays, rose to supranormal values by about age 30 years and appeared to increase further after that. Serum alkaline phosphatase and creatinine were normal, but inorganic phosphate was lower than in unaffected kindred members.
quotes: After identification of the proposita, 46 kindred members spanning 5 generations, ages 1.5 to 91 years, were surveyed biochemically and/or studied by chart review.

Of the 46 individuals studied, 19 were found to be affected. Serum iPTH levels, determined in three separate immunoassays, became supranormal by about age 30 years in the group of 15 hypercalcemic subjects examined biochemically and appeared to increase further thereafter.
Serum alkaline phosphatase activity and creatinine levels were normal in these individuals, but inorganic phosphate levels were lower than in unaffected kindred members.

phenotypes.text: elevated serum parathyroid hormone in adults

findings.statement: McMurtry et al. (1992) found that 3 of 5 affected adults older than 40 years who were studied radiographically had changes suggestive of osteomalacia. Iliac crest biopsy after tetracycline labeling in a 51-year-old affected woman confirmed defective skeletal mineralization. The authors suggested that the disorder may not be totally benign and that osteomalacia, perhaps due to mild hypophosphatemia, can develop in adulthood.
quotes: Three of five affected adults older than age 40 years who were studied radiographically had changes suggestive of osteomalacia.
Biopsy of the iliac crest of one of the subjects, a 51-year-old woman, confirmed the presence of defective skeletal mineralization.
Furthermore, the disorder may not be totally benign. Osteomalacia, perhaps due to mild hypophosphatemia, can develop during adulthood.

phenotypes.text: defective skeletal mineralization on bone biopsy

findings.statement: McMurtry et al. (1992) pointed out that in this kindred FBH in adults can be especially difficult to tell apart from primary hyperparathyroidism because serum PTH levels may be elevated. They suggested that the kindred might represent an unusual variant of FBH.
quotes: In this kindred, FBH in adults can be especially difficult to distinguish from primary hyperparathyroidism because serum iPTH levels may be elevated.
will help to clarify if we have observed an unusual variant of FBH.
